title_en: Guiding Case No. 238: Sheng v. Jiangsu Mou Network Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of labor relationship
ruling_gist_en:
1. Where a platform enterprise or a platform-employment cooperative enterprise requires a worker to register as an individual business household before signing a contract for work or a cooperation agreement, and the worker asserts that the labor relationship should be determined based on actual performance, the people's court shall, on the basis of ascertaining the facts and in accordance with relevant laws, accurately make a determination. Where there are facts of employment that constitute dominant labor management, the existence of a labor relationship shall be determined in accordance with the law.

2. Where there is subcontracting of the main business, the people's court shall, based on the facts of employment and the degree of labor management, and taking into account factors such as the actual entity responsible for labor management and the source of labor remuneration, determine in accordance with the law that the worker has established a labor relationship with the enterprise to which the worker is most closely connected.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 238

Sheng v. Jiangsu Mou Network Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of labor relationship

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 20, 2024)

Keywords

Civil; confirmation of labor relationship; new forms of employment; individual business; contracting and cooperation agreements; actual performance; labor management

Ruling Gist

1. Where a platform enterprise or a platform employment cooperation enterprise requires a worker to register as an individual business operator before signing a contracting or cooperation agreement, and the worker claims that the labor relationship should be determined based on the actual performance, the people's court shall, after ascertaining the facts, make an accurate determination in accordance with relevant laws. If there are facts of employment that constitute dominant labor management, the existence of a labor relationship shall be determined in accordance with the law.

2. Where the main business is subcontracted, the people's court shall, based on the facts of employment and the degree of labor management, and taking into account factors such as the actual entity responsible for labor management and the source of labor remuneration, determine in accordance with the law that the worker has established a labor relationship with the enterprise most closely connected with him or her.

Basic Facts

Jiangsu Mou Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangsu Mou Network Company) contracted the food delivery services for a certain food delivery platform in the Xushuguan area of Huqiu District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province. On April 25, 2019, Sheng registered as a dedicated delivery rider for the said platform in the Xushuguan area through a specific APP. The specific operational model for dedicated delivery riders was as follows: in terms of registration, dedicated delivery riders could only download and register the APP with authorization from the station; in terms of order assignment, the platform assigned orders to dedicated delivery riders based on their location, and riders could not refuse orders; if they were unable to accept orders due to special circumstances, they had to apply for order reassignment; in terms of rider management, dedicated delivery riders were managed by their exclusive station, and the station manager decided on order reassignment and rider scheduling, with riders required to go online to accept orders according to the schedule; in terms of salary composition and settlement, the salary of dedicated delivery riders included order commissions, rider subsidies, and other subsidies. During the registration process, Sheng underwent facial recognition and, following the prompts, said, "I want to become an individual business operator." Thereafter, Sheng accepted orders through the said APP and used his own vehicle for delivery after accepting orders. Jiangsu Mou Network Company had clear working hours and attendance requirements for Sheng, and deductions from corresponding rewards would be made for leave.

On May 30, 2019, Jiangsu Mou Network Company entered into a service agreement with Jiangsu Mou Enterprise Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangsu Mou Management Company), agreeing to entrust Jiangsu Mou Management Company with providing marketing promotion services; Jiangsu Mou Management Company could further subcontract after accepting project orders; if the person performing the tasks caused personal injury or property damage to themselves or any third party during the execution of the tasks, Jiangsu Mou Network Company should bear the consequences itself and could not require Jiangsu Mou Management Company to bear tort or other compensation liabilities; each month, the two parties would reconcile the list of persons performing the tasks, commission fees, service fees, etc., for the previous month, and Jiangsu Mou Network Company would deposit the corresponding funds into its account on a third-party platform, and the third-party platform would transfer the corresponding fees to the account of the person performing the tasks. On June 10 of the same year, Sheng entrusted Jiangsu Mou Management Company to register him as an "individual business operator," and signed a "Project Subcontracting Agreement" with Jiangsu Mou Management Company in the name of the "individual business operator," stipulating: the parties are independent civil contracting parties and do not have a labor relationship; the individual business operator independently contracts the delivery service business and bears all risks and liabilities that may arise during the contracting process; Jiangsu Mou Management Company settles service fees to the individual business operator on a monthly basis. On June 13 of the same year, Sheng was registered as an "individual business operator," with its business scope including marketing planning, marketing promotion services, and exhibition display services. From June to August 2019, Sheng received salaries of RMB 5,035.5, RMB 6,270.5, and RMB 5,807.7 respectively (currency unit: RMB). The salary bill page in the said APP showed that the salary rules were formulated by Jiangsu Mou Network Company, and the salary composition included base salary, commissions, subsidies and rewards, etc., with a base salary of RMB 0.

At approximately 10:00 p.m. on August 24, 2019, Sheng was injured in a traffic accident during the food delivery process. Disputing with Jiangsu Mou Network Company over the determination of work-related injury, Sheng applied for arbitration, seeking confirmation that a labor relationship existed between him and Jiangsu Mou Network Company from April 26, 2019, to August 24, 2019. The Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission of Huqiu District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province, ruled to dismiss Sheng's arbitration claim. Dissatisfied, Sheng filed a lawsuit with the Huqiu District People's Court of Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province. During the proceedings, the Huqiu District People's Court of Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province, ex officio added Jiangsu Mou Management Company as a third party to participate in the litigation.

Judgment

The Huqiu District People's Court of Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province, rendered a civil judgment (2020) Su 0505 Min Chu No. 5582 on August 2, 2021, holding that a labor relationship existed between Sheng and Jiangsu Mou Network Technology Co., Ltd. from April 25, 2019, to August 24, 2019. After the judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning

The focus of the dispute in this case is: whether a labor relationship existed between food delivery rider Sheng and Jiangsu Mou Network Company.

A labor relationship is a relationship established between an individual worker and an employer based on employment. However, in practice, there are cases where enterprises require workers to register as "individual business operators" before signing contracting or cooperation contracts to avoid establishing labor relationships with workers. When a dispute arises and the worker claims that a labor relationship exists with the enterprise, the people's court should not determine the relationship solely based on the contracting or cooperation agreement signed by the parties. Instead, it should comprehensively consider factors such as personal subordination, economic subordination, and organizational subordination based on the facts of employment, and accurately determine whether a labor relationship exists between the enterprise and the worker. The fact that a worker is required to register as an "individual business operator" does not preclude the establishment of a labor relationship with the employer. If there are facts of employment that constitute dominant labor management, the existence of a labor relationship shall be determined in accordance with the law.

In this case, Jiangsu Mou Network Company required food delivery rider Sheng to register as an "individual business operator" before signing a contracting or cooperation agreement with him, intending to avoid the legal responsibilities that the employer should bear. In reality, there was a strong personal subordination, economic subordination, and organizational subordination between the two parties, constituting dominant labor management. Specifically: (1) Sheng had to be authorized by the station to complete APP registration to become a dedicated delivery rider. Thereafter, Sheng accepted orders through the APP, received remuneration based on work performance, could not refuse orders assigned by the platform, and had to apply to Jiangsu Mou Network Company for order reassignment in special circumstances when unable to accept orders. Moreover, Jiangsu Mou Network Company formulated attendance rules and managed Sheng's daily work. (2) It could be seen from the salary rule explanations in the APP salary bill page and the platform service agreement that the source of Sheng's salary and the party formulating the salary rules was Jiangsu Mou Network Company, and the amount paid was determined by Jiangsu Mou Network Company, with the two parties actually settling the salary. (3) Sheng registered as a dedicated delivery rider, affiliated with the Xushuguan area station of a certain food delivery platform contracted by Jiangsu Mou Network Company, and the food delivery services he engaged in were part of the company's main business. In summary, Jiangsu Mou Network Company required and guided Sheng to register as an "individual business operator" in the form of establishing a so-called cooperative relationship between equal civil subjects to avoid employer responsibilities, but in fact there were facts of employment and dominant labor management over Sheng, which conformed to the essential characteristics of a labor relationship. Therefore, it should be determined that a labor relationship existed between the two parties.

Regarding the issue of whether Sheng had a labor relationship with Jiangsu Mou Network Company or with Jiangsu Mou Management Company. Upon investigation, although Jiangsu Mou Network Company subcontracted the delivery business to Jiangsu Mou Management Company by signing a platform service agreement, Sheng in fact continued to accept orders and make deliveries through the previously registered APP, and Jiangsu Mou Network Company also assigned orders and settled wages through the said APP. Sheng was directly assigned work, directly managed, and had his salary settled by Jiangsu Mou Network Company. The closeness of the connection between him and Jiangsu Mou Network Company was significantly stronger than that between him and Jiangsu Mou Management Company. Therefore, Jiangsu Mou Network Company's defense that no labor relationship existed between it and Sheng solely on the ground that there was an internal subcontracting relationship with Jiangsu Mou Management Company was not supported in accordance with the law.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 16 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China

Articles 7 and 10 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China
